title: There are no method ambiguities in `Advection`

body:
#5849 caused [out-of-bounds reads](https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl/issues/911) downstream in Breeze when using `GradientBoundaryCondition`.  CC @maximilian-gelbrecht.

> An array-valued boundary condition is evaluated as `condition[i, j, 1]`, which is right for a plain 2D array and for a `Field` reduced along the boundary-normal direction, but not for a `Field` windowed to a boundary plane with `indices`, e.g. `GradientBoundaryCondition(Field(-g * ρ, indices = (:, :, grid.Nz)))`: such a field stores its data offset to the window (its k-axis is `Nz:Nz`), so `[i, j, 1]` silently reads out of bounds under `@inbounds` (and throws a `BoundsError` with `--check-bounds=yes`). Nothing validated array-valued conditions either.
>
> Fields windowed to a single plane in one direction are now read at their own plane, in `getbc` methods dispatching on the `Field`'s indices type parameter, for the x, y and z boundaries. Their location and window are preserved when they are adapted for kernels, as is already done for reduced fields, so that these methods also dispatch on the GPU. `regularize_boundary_condition` now rejects a `Field` windowed to more than one plane, or windowed along a tangential direction, with an `ArgumentError`. Reduced fields and plain arrays behave as before.

Fix https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl/issues/911.
title: Read Field boundary conditions windowed to a plane at their own plane
